name: Nguma-Monene
body:
NGUMA-MONENE
CR 12

This huge, long-bodied aquatic lizard has serrated scales of grayish brown along its back and light brown underneath, with massive crocodilian jaws.

XP 19,200
N Gargantuan animal (aquatic)
Init +12; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +15

DEFENSE

AC 31, touch 19, flat-footed 18 (+12 Dex, +1 Dodge, +12 natural, -4 size)
hp 174 (17d8+102)
Fort +16, Ref +22, Will +10
Defensive Abilities elusive

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., swim 40 ft.
Melee bite +20 (4d6+6 plus grab), 4 claws +20 (1d8+6)
Space 20 ft.; Reach 20 ft.
Special Attacks capsize, constrict (4d6+6), strangle

STATISTICS

Str 23, Dex 34, Con 23, Int 2, Wis 21, Cha 9
Base Atk +12; CMB +22 (+26 drag and grapple); CMD 44 (can’t be tripped)
Feats Acrobatic Steps, Dodge, Lightning Stance, Mobility, Nimble Moves, Skill Focus (Stealth), Spring Attack, Weapon Finesse, Wind Stance
Skills Perception +15, Stealth +12, Swim +34; Racial Modifiers +12 Stealth, +12 Swim

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Capsize (Ex)

A nguma-monene can attempt to capsize a Gargantuan or smaller boat with a combat maneuver check (DC 25 or the result of the boat pilot’s Profession (sailor) check, if higher).

Drag to the Deeps (Ex)

When swimming and using Spring Attack, a nguma-monene need not move prior to attacking, and if it hits a Huge or smaller creature it can make a combat maneuver check as a free action to drag the target. It can drag a creature 5 feet even if it has no movement remaining.

Elusive (Su)

Nguma-monene are almost never caught even by survivors. As a full-round action, it can move up to 200 feet and make a Stealth check to hide with a +40 circumstance bonus. It leaves no tracks, as if using pass without trace. It also gains the effect of nondetection (caster level 20th) when not in combat; neither spell effect can be dispelled.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm aquatic (freshwater)
Organization solitary
Treasure none

The nguma-monene (or “ripping python”) is an immense aquatic lizard strong enough to kill a hippopotamus with ease or snatch a cape buffalo from the waterside before its herd even notices it is missing. The creature’s body is 5 feet wide, giving it an almost serpentine appearance, but it can greatly distend its belly to more than double that size when it has gorged itself on bulky prey and settles into deep underwater mud banks to sleep off its meal.

The nguma-monenen is an elusive creature that prefers to remain hidden most of the time. It rarely exposes its entire bulk, cunningly using vegetation and water to hide its movements and keeping most of its body shielded underwater when fighting aerial or terrestrial foes. While not obvious from outside the water, the nguma-monene has four stump-like legs that extend perpendicularly to its body and end in clawed toes, which can propel it with surprising quickness and agility even across rough terrain.
